title: Leveraging Affirmation
coreMove: Praise is a leadership tool when it is specific, shared quickly, and used to show people which behaviors matter.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Validation from people you respect lands hardest, and witnessing it can transform how an entire team sees its own worth.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the lesson to this situation without copying a surface gesture.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A leader who absorbs all the credit starves the team of the recognition that actually drives them; deflecting the spotlight is the higher-leverage move.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the lesson to this situation without copying a surface gesture.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Praise that comes from outside the organization is more powerful than praise handed down from a boss.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Routing reporters, PR requests, and compliments to the person who runs a given program turns ordinary staff into recognized specialists.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Letting people become celebrated, even at the risk that competitors will try to poach them, is worth it because the upside in motivation and reputation outweighs the loss.
